overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Town Meeting postponement was an unanticipated topic, the draft minutes were not reviewed because they were in draft form, and the Board was reminded about timely minute approval.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board voted to postpone Annual Town Meeting at its March 23, 2018 meeting though the topic was not listed on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the topic was unanticipated by the chair and thus the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by discussing and voting on the postponement of Town Meeting during this meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the draft minutes of the March 23, 2018 meeting were inaccurate or insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: Because the minutes were in draft form at the time this complaint was filed, we decline to review their sufficiency.

allegations.summary: Not raised by complainant: AG noted the March 23 minutes were approved May 1, later than the timely-approval deadline, and reminded the Board of the requirement.
allegations.key_passage: The Board should have approved the March 23, 2018 meeting minutes by its third subsequent meeting, on April 23, 2018.
